findings.title: Drop queries that become empty during interpolation
findings.body: The empty-expression filter runs before `applyTemplateVariables`. A target such as `expr: '$optionalQuery'` can therefore become `''` after its variable is resolved, but is still classified and sent to Loki as a split metric/log query. This produces unnecessary requests and can surface backend parse errors for dashboards that intentionally use an empty optional query. Filter the interpolated targets again (or interpolate before filtering).

findings.title: Shard-split requests interpolate template filters twice
findings.body: `runShardSplitQuery` interpolates each target here, then passes the resulting sharded `subRequest` to `runSplitQuery`, which now calls `datasource.applyTemplateVariables` again for every shard group. The second call receives the same `request.filters`; template application is not generally safe to repeat, particularly when dashboard/ad-hoc filters are injected into the LogQL selector, so filters can be duplicated or the query can be altered/invalid. Interpolate only once for a sharded execution, or ensure the nested time-splitting path does not reapply template variables to already interpolated targets.

findings.title: Shard splitting no longer ignores targets interpolated to an empty expression
findings.body: The previous flow interpolated targets before filtering out empty expressions, whereas this change filters `query.expr` before `applyTemplateVariables`. If a variable-backed expression resolves to an empty string, it is retained and proceeds through shard selector discovery and the nested split query, potentially issuing invalid empty LogQL requests instead of behaving as a disabled/empty target. Filter the mapped targets for a non-empty `expr` before calling `splitQueriesByStreamShard`.
